research.officialTopicTextPolicy: Paraphrase and link official curriculum; do not copy exam questions, passages, rubrics, or exhaustive CED prose into the artifact.
research.exhaustiveCedObjectivesAuthority: The linked course-and-exam-description source for each course.

generalScoring: Multiple-choice raw score is based on correct responses.
Free-response and performance work are scored with course-specific criteria.
Component scores are combined and converted to a 1–5 AP score using College Board standard-setting processes.

notes: Biology, Chemistry, Physics, economics, statistics, and graphing-calculator math exams have course-specific permissions. Check the course exam record and current College Board calculator policy before displaying student-facing guidance.

terms.stimulusSet: A group of related questions tied to shared text, data, image, map, model, or other material.
terms.hybridDigital: Students use Bluebook for the digital portion and handwrite free-response answers in paper booklets.
terms.fullyDigital: Students complete and submit all documented exam responses in Bluebook.
terms.performanceTask: A through-course project or performance component that contributes to the AP score.

validationNotes: Diagram is a nullable semantic DiagramSpec encoded as a JSON string at the model boundary and parsed before persistence.

generationRules: Stay strictly within the selected unit keywords and topics.
Do not repeat recent topics when recent-topic context is available.
Use original content and do not reconstruct an identifiable College Board question.
Return only the validated JSON object.

validationRules: IDs use stable label characters and length limits.
Section IDs and rubric criterion IDs are unique.
Each criterion references a known section.
Criterion levels have unique points including zero and reach maxPoints.
Each section rubric total equals section maxPoints.
Responses are text-only and bounded by section and total character limits.

generationRules: Keep rubric facts private from the student payload.
Persist course and unit metadata with the question.

generation.courseGuidance: Frame questions around experimental or data-based scenarios; emphasize evolution/natural selection evidence, energy transfer, cell communication, and gene expression/regulation. Use correct biology terminology and simple quantitative tools (chi-square, Hardy–Weinberg reasoning) without heavy math. Avoid anatomy trivia not in the framework. Avoid Chemistry and physics equations and instead focus on biological concepts.

frq.generationGuidance: Create an original data-rich scientific analysis task focused on causal reasoning, evidence interpretation, and experimental or quantitative justification. Use text, Markdown tables, and LaTeX only.
frq.gradingGuidance: Award points only for biologically correct claims connected to evidence or mechanisms; definitions alone do not earn application or reasoning points.
